units.translation: And Ares is a bitter, evil divider of wealth.
The choice flower of many riches.
From this man's wealth I will try to rule the citizens.
But Orestes is in exile from his wealth.
A great share of the captive wealth.
An Argive man again dwells in his ancestral wealth.
When wealth is plundered from the house, other wealth may come by the grace of Zeus the protector of possessions.
He has died, a shameful cheat of wealth.
A bitter distributor of possessions, a savage-minded iron.
The wise man is he who knows useful things, not he who knows many things.
Such an oracle the ancient mother related to me.
Alas, swift has come the fulfillment of the oracles.
And indeed the oracle will no longer look out from under veils.
You have entered upon this oracle with truth.
In such oracles, then, must we trust?
Zeus, as you say, sent this oracle.
And I bid you to fear my oracles and those of Zeus.
This prophecy is no longer easy to interpret.
oracle, temple where oracles are given; victim
Explained as ἱερεῖον [sacrificial victim] by the grammarians cited in the Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 1671.
It is not right for pollution to be worn away in these nearby oracles.
In the Pythian oracles at the navel of the earth.
It is for men to perform these slaughters and sacrifices to the gods.
One must greatly sacrifice and many victims must fall to many gods.
oracular, prophetic, giving oracles; sent from an oracle
Having been brought forth in oracular houses.
Preserving the oracular commands of Loxias.
Let the good things be accomplished.
that with which something is anointed

Concerning oil, where some copies have χρίσματος [of anointing], which is a later form, not better than κέχρισμαι [I have been anointed], which is sometimes read in manuscripts for κέχριμαι [I have been anointed]: see Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 1683.
A torch rises, prepared with pure ointment, with soft, guileless soothing.
Aorist infinitive with apocope. For thus I corrected what is read in M: πρὶν τῷδ᾽ ἐχριμφθῆν χροῖν [before this one to touch the skin]; about which see under χρώς [skin].
Bringing her foot near the sea-resounding cliffs.
It is not fitting to approach these houses.
Before this one (or thus) to touch the skin.
before this one to touch the skin
Of medicines that are applied by anointing.
There was no remedy, neither edible, nor for anointing, nor trustworthy.
Again some gadfly stings me, wretched as I am.
It wastes me, stinging with maddening goads.
The point of the gadfly stings me, without fire.
